title: feat(spec,objectql,metadata-protocol)!: one default record page per object per deployment, a second refused at os validate, registration and save (#23015)
body:
Fixes #23015
Clause-②: yes (narrowing: a second default record page for one object, accepted today, is refused; the public surface also grows by the new `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` code and the new exports, per contract review 6142059579)

Ruling A (record 6134056653) on #23015, quoted from the card: "**A — one default record page per object per deployment, refused loudly.** The spec states that at most one `isDefault: true` record page may exist for an object in a deployment. A second is refused at registration and at save, naming both holders, the way ADR-0048's 2026-10-08 addendum refuses a second holder of a position, permission-set or capability name. The renderer then honours `isDefault` with no tie-break."

This PR is the objectstack half. It changes nothing in objectui or cloud. Their seats file those legs (objectstack-ai/objectui#12195, and the cloud card the ruling asks for).

## Census: every `isDefault: true` record page producer

Measured on objectstack `1a6e24c99` (this branch after merging `origin/main` `e540e7ffb`; the producer set is unchanged at `b091cd851`) and objectui `4baa8a67c`. A producer is non-test source that ships a record page (`type: 'record'`, or no `type`) bound to an object and declared `isDefault: true`.

| repo | object | page | producer |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| objectstack | `sys_organization` | `sys_organization_detail` | `@objectstack/plugin-auth` (`SysOrganizationDetailPage`) |
| objectstack | `sys_user` | `sys_user_detail` | `@objectstack/plugin-auth` (`SysUserDetailPage`) |
| objectstack | `sys_position` | `sys_position_detail` | `@objectstack/plugin-security` (`SysPositionDetailPage`) |
| objectstack | `sys_approval_request` | `sys_approval_request_detail` | `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` |
| objectstack | `showcase_project` | `showcase_project_detail` | `examples/app-showcase` |
| objectstack | `showcase_task` | `showcase_task_detail` | `examples/app-showcase` |
| objectstack | `showcase_preference` | `showcase_settings` | `examples/app-showcase` |
| objectui | none | none | 0 record-page producers. The `isDefault: true` hits are apps, flow edges and list views. |

Every object has exactly one default, so no producer in either repository trips the refusal. The fork clause does not fire here.

`isDefault: true` on a page that is not a record page bound to an object is outside the rule. The one case of that is `showcase_capability_map`, a `home` page. It is unchanged.

**The carried producer is the cloud leg.** cloud's `cloud_organization_detail` (`com.objectstack.service-tenant`) and plugin-auth's `sys_organization_detail` are both defaults for `sys_organization`. A cloud boot on an engine that carries this PR will be refused with `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` and both pages named. The ruling orders the cloud leg to land before cloud bumps to that engine, and the cloud seat resolves it. cloud is not in this session, so this run did not re-measure it. The pair is the card's own measurement.

**The cloud seat needs one measured fact.** An environment save under a page that a **managed package ships** is refused before this rule is reached, with `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` 403: `page` is `allowEnvironmentOverlay: false`, which is the ADR-0126 Regime C rollback. The `default-record-page-save-door.test.ts` control pins this on both topologies, unchanged. So "overlay `sys_organization_detail` by name" is not available as an environment save. For cloud, the paths that remain are host composition (compose plugin-auth without its organization page) and not shipping a second default. The ruling's fork clause routes a lost-behaviour finding to the cloud seat, so this is reported and the ruling is not touched.

## FROM → TO, per door

All three doors judge with one reading: `defaultRecordPageObject(page)` (`@objectstack/spec/ui`, `default-record-page.ts`). It holds the type default (`PAGE_TYPE_DEFAULT`) that `PageSchema.type` is now built from.

| door | FROM | TO |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `defineStack`, and so `os validate`, `os build` and a source boot | two default record pages for one object in `pages` accepted. The boot kept both, and registration order picked the one that opened. | refused, `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` 422. The finding names the object and every page with its position: `Object 'X' has two default record pages in \`pages\`: 'a' (stack.pages[0]) and 'b' (stack.pages[1]). Set \`isDefault: false\` on all but one of them. …` |
| `composeStacks` | each input legal on its own, so the pair composed clean | refused in the same envelope, naming each stack's page. Under `manifest: 'preserve'`, one page name in two stacks counts as two packages' pages. |
| package registration (`SchemaRegistry.installPackage`, ahead of every mutation, and the `registerItem` seam) | a second package, a nested plugin or a plugin's `manifest.register` shipping a default for an object another package holds registered silently | refused, `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` 422 (new ledger code, exported `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT_CODE`), with `object`, `incoming`, `existing` and `conflicts`: `Default record page conflict: page "b" of package "p2" cannot be the default record page of object "X": page "a" of package "p1" already is. …` The other holder can be another package's page (two packages' pages under one name are two pages), the environment's stored page, or a second page of the same manifest. No `collisionPolicy` downgrade. |
| metadata save (`saveMetaItem`, so `PUT /api/v1/meta/page/:name`) | a page saved `isDefault: true` for an object that already had a default stored or shipped was accepted | refused, `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` 422, in draft and publish mode, before anything is written. The message names both pages and gives the remedy that applies: demote the stored default, or for a shipped page, compose without the package. The holders are the environment-wide stored rows plus `SchemaRegistry.defaultRecordPageHoldersOf(object)`, so an environment-scoped kernel (no write-through) is judged too. |

**What is not a second default**, pinned at each door:
- a save under the existing default's own name (an ADR-0005 overlay by name);
- an environment item under the registered page's own name;
- the same package again: a reload, or an upgrade that moves its default to another of its own pages;
- a non-default record page;
- defaults for two different objects;
- an `isDefault` page that is not a record page.

**Also in this diff:**
- The page form's `isDefault` help used to say "Set as default page for this page type", which is a rule nothing enforced. It now states this rule. The source is `page.form.ts`; the `en` bundle leaf was hand-edited to the source's string, and the `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES` leaves were hand-translated.
- The hand-written `content/docs/ui/pages.mdx` row said the same thing and is corrected too.
- `PageSchema.isDefault` gets its `.describe()`. The regenerated reference docs, `api-surface/ui.json` and `export-origins/ui.json` each add one row.
- The D3 entry is `18.page-default-record-page-one-per-object-refused` (no `relevantWhen`, because the surface reaches plugin code and stored rows).
- `DEFAULT_RECORD_PAGE_CONFLICT` is registered under `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`. It has its own code rather than `NAMESPACE_CONFLICT`. No name is taken: what is held is an object's one default slot, and renaming fixes nothing.

The objectql suite reads `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` through `dist/`, so the package was rebuilt, and `ablation-dist-preflight` confirmed the marker present before, absent after, and present again on restore, with the tree clean. | 6 failed / 20 | 20/20 |

## Acceptance notes

- **A boundary of the registry door, stated in the module doc and not closed here:** `sys_metadata` hydration is not judged. That is the bare slot, with no package, which is the same thing ADR-0048 N.3 says for the security catalog. The save door refuses a second default before it is stored. But at a cold boot every package registers before stored pages hydrate. So a stored default saved while no package held that object's default, together with a package upgrade that later adds one, reaches the registry unrefused on restart. A hot install of that package is refused. Closing the cold-boot order would mean refusing a boot after hydration. The security catalog got that only by its own ruling (#22307), so it is not invented here. Carrier: none.
- `isDefault` on `home` / `app` / `utility` / `list` pages keeps whatever objectui does with it today. The ruling's words are "record page for an object", and only those are judged.
- The save door judges environment-wide rows, per ADR-0131 D6, because an organization-scoped write is refused for every type. A draft is judged twice: at its own save, and again when it is published (`promoteDraftForPublish`, which covers both `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts`). Another page may have taken the default in between; a test pins that case.
